_: Sixty seconds of Flamme Retardé, in four shots of three chunks each.
The arithmetic is the whole shape of this file. Wan generates 81 frames at
a time and nothing can change that, so a 60 s film is twelve independent
jobs — and the one place a seam between two independently generated chunks
is invisible is a cut. So every shot is a whole number of chunks (243 = 3 x
81 = 15.19 s), the three cuts land exactly on chunk boundaries 3, 6 and 9,
and the eight seams left over are inside a continuous take where the same
seed and the same prompt are holding them together.
It also buys the thing the restyle notebook calls the obvious next lever
and has never done: a prompt per shot. At cfg 1.0 the positive prompt is
the entire text conditioning, and one prompt cannot describe both an
aeroplane over a burning hillside and a bathing terrace. See
tools/lab/demo60-prompts.sh.

shots.name: runin
_: The run-in, from the sea. No `per` at all: this is the game's own chase
camera, which is a spring behind a flight model, and hand-animating a
camera that follows an aeroplane looks exactly like hand-animating a
camera that follows an aeroplane.
Placed 2.5 km short of the ignition point on a bearing of 68 deg, which
puts the coast across the middle of the frame and the smoke column dead
ahead. At 92 m/s the shot covers 1.4 km and never arrives, on purpose:
the aeroplane is still closing when the cut comes.

shots.name: drop
_: Over the fire, on the close camera, and the load goes down at 5.6 s.
The drop is driven by a synthetic keydown rather than by a handle, and
that is worth a note because the file says twice that it cannot be:
`input.drop` is recomputed every frame from `keys.has('KeyF')`, and a
dispatched KeyboardEvent does reach that set. What does not reach it is
anything dispatched BEFORE the pause, because `setPaused` clears it.
shots.per: if (i === 90) window.dispatchEvent(new KeyboardEvent('keydown', {code: 'KeyF', bubbles: true})); if (i === 152) window.dispatchEvent(new KeyboardEvent('keyup', {code: 'KeyF', bubbles: true}));

shots.name: prom
_: The bathing terrace, walked west to east past the kabine.
This is the shot the restyle notebook says works — architecture,
vegetation and skin in one frame, with real parallax down a row of
buildings, which is where temporal coherence either holds or gives the
game away. 48 m in 15.2 s is 3.2 m/s, which is a brisk walk and about
twice what a dolly would do; slower reads as a real camera but leaves
the whole shot on four huts.
Eye at 1.62 m off the promenade deck, looking 14 m ahead and a little
inland so the row runs across the frame rather than away down it.
shots.per: (() => { const J = __fr.jad.raw(); const t = 296 + T * 3.16; const a = J.toWorld(t, 10.6); const c = J.toWorld(t + 14, 15.4); __fr.look(a[0], a[1] + 1.62, a[2], c[0], c[1] + 1.15, c[2]); })()

shots.name: brod
_: Out along the Brod, ending on Tvrdava svetog Nikole.
The pier runs on a bearing of 55.5 deg from a root at (-1770.5, 328.5);
the causeway behind it ramps from the shelf up to the 1.15 m deck over
30 m, and the camera height follows that ramp rather than floating over
it. 46 m of walk in 15.2 s.
The aim eases from 'along the pier' to 'the fortress' over the shot, so
it opens on the boat lying alongside and closes on the thing the whole
side quest is pointed at, 646 m away across the channel.
shots.per: (() => { const b = 55.5 * Math.PI / 180, ax = Math.sin(b), az = -Math.cos(b); const u = -26 + T * 4.6; const x = -1770.5 + ax * u, z = 328.5 + az * u; const deck = u < 0 ? 0.10 + (1.15 - 0.10) * (u + 30) / 30 : 1.15; const k = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, (T - 4) / 8)); const hx = -1770.5 + ax * (u + 60), hz = 328.5 + az * (u + 60); const tx = hx + (-1237.2 - hx) * k, tz = hz + (718.5 - hz) * k; __fr.look(x, deck + 1.62, z, tx, deck + 1.0 + 14 * k, tz); })()
